title: Trivial norm-scalar cyclic restriction and its finite biproducts
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, and $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$. On the coherent profinite site in the compatible universes of [def-weil-size-convention], put $A(S)=C(S,F)$, with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its inverse-limit topology, $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$, $u(k)=k$, and $\tau=u(1)=1$. Use ordinary internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with condensed $H$-actions [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], their ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $H$-invariants taken in the full action category. Write
$$c_N=(\lambda_N^1)^{-1}\beta_N^1:R\Gamma_H(N[0])\longrightarrow Q[N\xrightarrow{\tau-1}N]$$
for the invariant-normalized cyclic restriction comparison of [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model], with residual group trivial and cyclic degrees $0,1$.

Give $A$ the trivial $H$-action. Let $U_A^q(S)=C(S\times H^q,F)$ for $q\geq0$, zero for $q<0$, with the trivial-action inhomogeneous group differential. Let $\mathscr B_A(H)=\operatorname{Tot}_{q\geq0}R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline H^q],A[0])$, where $A[\underline H^q]$ is the free internal module on $S\mapsto C(S,H^q)$ and Hom is derived in the second variable using compatible nonnegative resolutions. Let $j_A:QU_A^\bullet\to\mathscr B_A(H)$ be the actual resolution augmentation and $\eta:R\Gamma_H(A[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr B_A(H)$ the invariant-normalized derived-bar identification [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. Define $\epsilon:U_A^\bullet\to[A\xrightarrow0 A]$ by the identity in degree zero, evaluation at $1$ in degree one, and zero in higher degrees. Then $j_A$ and $c_A$ are isomorphisms, with
$$c_A\eta^{-1}j_A=Q\epsilon.$$
For every finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $W$ with trivial $H$-action, including $W=0$, the canonical comparison $c_{C(-,F\otimes_E W)}$ is an isomorphism. The tensor extension has its finite-dimensional product norm topology. All statements use ordinary internal modules; for $F=\Omega$ no completeness or termwise internal-Hom acyclicity is asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-procyclic-scalar-cochain-evaluation] with the stated $\ell,\Omega,E,F$. Its function sheaves, differential and evaluation morphism are exactly $U_A^\bullet$ and $\epsilon$ here. It gives a quasi-isomorphism of sheaf complexes for both $F=E$ and $F=\Omega$, with ordinary kernel/image cohomology. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], localization therefore makes $Q\epsilon$ invertible. No objectwise existence of primitives is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent assembly of the existing scalar analytic and invariant-normalization inputs.

proof.text: First take $F=E$. In the compatible nonnegative resolution model of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar], regard $U_A^\bullet$ as the double complex supported in resolution degree zero. For each bar degree $q$, apply [lem-sfb-normed-scalar-profinite-hom-acyclic] to the profinite set $P=H^q$. Its evaluation-normalized canonical resolution comparison is precisely this column of the augmentation. Thus every column map is a quasi-isomorphism. Both double complexes are first quadrant, and each total degree has finitely many summands. By [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] their actual total map is a quasi-isomorphism. Its localization is the specified $j_A$, so $j_A$ is invertible. Completeness is used only through the cited theorem for the finite field $E$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent assembly of the existing scalar analytic and invariant-normalization inputs.

proof.text: For $F=\Omega$, apply [lem-sfb-norm-algcl-bar-augmentation]. Its source is the same continuous-function complex, its target is the same compatible derived bar total, and its map is induced by the coefficient-resolution augmentation in every bar degree. Hence it states invertibility of the actual $j_A$ used here. This application does not use the complete-field column assertion of step 2.

proof.text: In [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model] specialize $R=A$, residual group $G=1$, and $u(k)=k$. Its final identity is exactly $c_A\eta^{-1}j_A=Q\epsilon$, because $u(1)=1$ and the action on $A$ is trivial. The bar identification $\eta$ is invertible by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. Combining this identity with steps 1--3 gives $c_A=(Q\epsilon)j_A^{-1}\eta$, a composite of isomorphisms. This proves the asserted map equality as well as invertibility of $c_A$.

proof.text: Let $d=\dim_E W$ and choose an $E$-basis $w_1,\ldots,w_d$. In the stipulated finite-dimensional product norm topology, the coordinate identification $F\otimes_E W\cong F^d$, $\sum_i a_i\otimes w_i\mapsto(a_i)_i$, is a homeomorphism. Continuous maps into a finite product are exactly tuples of continuous coordinate maps. Consequently, on every profinite $S$, $C(S,F\otimes_E W)\cong C(S,F)^d$ by these formulas, compatibly with restriction and $A(S)$-scalars. This identifies the internal module $N=C(-,F\otimes_E W)$ with the finite biproduct $A^d$ with trivial action. For $d=0$, both sides are the zero module, including on the empty parameter set.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent assembly of the existing scalar analytic and invariant-normalization inputs.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], $R\Gamma_H$ is additive; the two-term zero-differential functor $K(N)=[N\xrightarrow0N]$ is additive term by term. Naturality of $c$ is supplied by [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model]. For the coordinate inclusions $i_i:A\to N$ and projections $p_i:N\to A$, define $b:QK(N)\to R\Gamma_H(N[0])$ by $b=\sum_i R\Gamma_H(i_i)c_A^{-1}QK(p_i)$. Naturality and $\sum_i i_ip_i=1_N$ give $c_Nb=\sum_i QK(i_i)QK(p_i)=1$ and $bc_N=\sum_i R\Gamma_H(i_i)R\Gamma_H(p_i)=1$. Thus the canonical $c_N$ is invertible. The empty sum gives the same equations for $d=0$, since additive functors preserve the zero identity. Although coordinates describe this inverse, the morphism being inverted is the canonical comparison, so the conclusion is independent of the basis.

The delivery adds no new nodes. I read all six steps against the cited statements. Step 1: lem-sfb-procyclic-scalar-cochain-evaluation has the same U_F, differential and ε, and states that ε is a quasi-isomorphism for F=E and F=Ω, so Qε is invertible. Step 2 (F=E): normed-scalar-profinite-hom-acyclic applies with E finite over Q_ℓ and P=Z_ℓ^q (q=0 is the point). Its statement gives the evaluation-normalized column comparison, and the generic first-quadrant node then gives the total quasi-isomorphism. That generic node is the declared tool use, which I accept. Step 3 (F=Ω): norm-algcl-bar-augmentation states that the actual j_A is invertible, without completeness. Step 4: the final clause of relative-cyclic-restriction-model with G=1, u(k)=k and u(1)=1 gives c_A η⁻¹ j_A = Qε; with η invertible, c_A = Qε j_A⁻¹ η, which I checked. Step 5 is elementary because the item stipulates the product norm topology, and it covers d=0 and S empty. Step 6: RΓ is additive (infrastructure node) and c is natural, and I checked that the explicit inverse satisfies both composite identities, including d=0. As an advisory only, the additivity of Q is cited in step 1 rather than step 6; it is already in proof_deps. There is no cycle: no proof_dep closure reaches the item. The duplicate scan found only the conditional sibling lem-sfb-nilpotent-restriction-devissage, and the blueprint scan found lem-exc-procyclic-two-term, which is discrete and torsion, so neither duplicates the item. I read blueprint main-20261015 paragraph (3) of the direct-images proof, identical to latest; there is no SGA citation. Batch 5: the spectral-norm leaf (Mathlib SpectralNorm) and Stacks 04BL (the free-module sheaf universal property) are generic facts outside the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality assumptions, so I accept them. No changes.
